title: Predicting Absorption-Distribution Properties of Neuroprotective Phosphine-Borane Compounds Using In Silico Modeling and Machine Learning
summary: Machine-learning and in-silico models estimated absorption/distribution properties of phosphine-borane compounds from lipid, permeability and related features. The neural networks predicted properties of known boron-containing compounds; pharmacokinetic and clinical validation of new candidates was not established.
ai_technology: In-silico machine-learning/QSAR models predict absorption-distribution properties of phosphine-borane compounds.
organization: Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences, McGill University, Montreal, QC H4H 3S5, Canada.

evidence.tested: Neural-network and in-silico models predicted pharmacokinetic properties of known boron-containing compounds, including phosphine-borane candidates.
evidence.unknown: Predictions for known compounds do not establish experimental pharmacokinetics for newly proposed candidates or clinical efficacy.
evidence.ai_role: In-silico machine-learning/QSAR models predict absorption-distribution properties of phosphine-borane compounds.
